# fivenines_docker_containers (Data Source)

The per-container state rows behind the instance's Containers tab -- which container is restart-looping, what it exited with, and whether the kernel OOM-killed it.

A row is keyed by container NAME, the durable identity: a `docker compose up` recreate mints a new `container_id` and keeps the name. `health` is null when the image defines no HEALTHCHECK -- not applicable, never a passing verdict -- and `restarts_last_24h` counts genuine crash-restarts only, since a manual `docker restart` does not bump the daemon's counter.

Container rows need agent >= 1.11.2. On an older agent the list is empty and `collector.supported` is false -- check it before reading an empty list as "no containers".

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_docker_containers" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.web.id
}

# Restart-looping containers. restarts_last_24h counts genuine crash-restarts
# only, and is a floor for a sustained loop -- treat it as "at least this many".
output "restart_looping" {
  value = [
    for c in data.fivenines_docker_containers.all.docker_containers :
    c.name if c.restarts_last_24h > 3
  ]
}

# health is null when the image defines no HEALTHCHECK -- not a passing verdict.
output "unhealthy" {
  value = [
    for c in data.fivenines_docker_containers.all.docker_containers :
    c.name if c.health == "unhealthy"
  ]
}

# Container rows need agent >= 1.11.2. On an older agent the list is empty.
output "container_rows_unavailable_because" {
  value = data.fivenines_docker_containers.all.collector.unavailable_reason
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `health` (String) Filter by HEALTHCHECK verdict. `none` selects the containers whose image defines no HEALTHCHECK -- a real, distinct state that the row carries as a null `health`, and one that neither `healthy` nor `unhealthy` would return. One of: `starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`, `none`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the container name or its image.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over the collector's 10-minute sync window. `false` returns only rows the agent refreshed inside it -- the set you may read as CURRENT state; `true` returns the rest. The two values partition the collection (a row that never synced counts as stale). Omit for both.
- `status` (String) Filter by the container's lifecycle state, in the `docker inspect` State.Status vocabulary. One of: `unknown`, `created`, `running`, `paused`, `restarting`, `removing`, `exited`, `dead`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `docker_containers` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--docker_containers))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--docker_containers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `docker_containers`

Read-Only:

- `container_id` (String) The runtime id, which CHANGES on a recreate. `name` is the stable key.
- `cpu_percent` (Number) CPU use at the last tick. **Null means no sample, not idle.**
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `exit_code` (Number) Null for a container that never exited -- not the same as exit code 0.
- `finished_at` (String) When the container last exited. Null for one that never has -- not the same as "exited just now".
- `health` (String) HEALTHCHECK verdict. **Null means the image defines no HEALTHCHECK** -- not-applicable, never a passing result. One of: `starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `image` (String) The image reference the container was started from, e.g. `nginx:1.27`. Null when not reported.
- `image_id` (String) The `sha256:` config digest, for joining to image-level findings.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `memory_limit` (Number) Bytes. Null when the container is unlimited.
- `memory_usage` (Number) Bytes.
- `name` (String) The container name. This is the durable identity: a `docker compose up` recreate mints a new `container_id` and keeps the name, so the row follows the name.
- `oom_killed` (Boolean) Whether the kernel OOM-killed the container on its last exit.
- `restart_count` (Number) The daemon's cumulative RestartCount.
- `restarts_last_24h` (Number) Restart-policy restarts in the trailing 24 hours -- the restart-loop signal. Counted from genuine crash-restarts only: a manual `docker restart` does not bump the daemon's counter. **A FLOOR, not an exact count, for a sustained loop:** the ingester keeps at most the 100 most recent increment events per container, so a container restarting every minute for a day reports roughly the last 100 of them. Treat a high value as "at least this many"; it is the same number the dashboard shows.
- `stale` (Boolean) True when the agent has not refreshed this row inside the 10-minute window.
- `started_at` (String) When the container last started. Null for one that never has.
- `state_changed_at` (String) When `status` last flipped. The field to poll for state transitions.
- `state_detail` (String) Human summary, e.g. `exited (code 137, OOM killed)`.
- `status` (String) The container's lifecycle state, in the `docker inspect` State.Status vocabulary, stored verbatim. `unknown` is what a value outside the pinned contract normalizes to. One of: `unknown`, `created`, `running`, `paused`, `restarting`, `removing`, `exited`, `dead`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
